title: Review: SSE stall-warn and peer-node logging
notes:
Maintainer risk: LOW — the behavioral change is correct and narrow (warn log on stall). The two P1 issues are naming confusion and a Headscale edge-case that makes the warn unactionable, neither of which causes data loss or security exposure. No correctness bugs found.
Confidence: 5% chance of missed bug. Uncertainty driven by: the coalescing task's lifecycle after sending the None sentinel (it loops back to select\! and exits via live_tx.closed() — correct, but the interaction was traced manually not via test). The Full-channel warning path is also untested. Would raise confidence if: a test exercised the Full path (requires a mock mpsc channel that reports Full on demand, or saturating the channel with 256 items before sending a broadcast) and if the post-None-sentinel task-exit path had a dedicated test. Both are non-trivial to test without a test-only hook.
